pages.text: The $(bold)Great White Space$() is a strange extradimensional space linking places light-years apart; the Elder Things built at least one gate to it on Earth.$(br2)It has only $(bold)two layers$(): bedrock at y=0, and one whole layer of $(bold)unbreakable white blocks$() at y=1. Its sky $(bold)never changes$() - always white.

A gate $(bold)changes colour with the dimension$(): one opened inside the Great White Space is $(bold)black$() (a near-black body with a pale silver rim - a white gate is nearly invisible on an all-white background), while one opened $(bold)anywhere else$() is $(bold)white$().$(br2)Both are the same gate - only the texture differs.

$(bold)Getting there$(): right-click a block with a $(l:white_space_pass)Dimension Pass$() to open a $(bold)2-tall$() gate above it, then walk in.$(br2)Gates always come $(bold)in pairs$() - one on each side, pointing at each other - so you can always walk back the way you came.

$(bold)This is a hub$(): inside the White Space, use the pass on a block again to get the $(bold)free mode$() screen - $(bold)pick a dimension$() and $(bold)type xyz$(), and a gate opens above the block you used.$(br2)The dropdown lists only $(bold)dimensions you have visited$().

$(bold)A few rules$(): $(li)gates teleport $(bold)players and other creatures$() (dropped items pass straight through, and a rider travels with its mount); $(li)if there is $(bold)no ground under your feet$() when you arrive, a $(bold)3x3 obsidian platform$() is placed for you; $(li)the landing point is $(bold)recorded automatically$() - if the far gate is broken, it is rebuilt on arrival.

$(bold)Removing a gate$(): gates are $(bold)unbreakable$() (hardness -1, like bedrock; blasts do nothing). Right-click one with a $(l:tool_tian_ni_huo)Heavenly Reverse Spear$() to tear down the whole gate, with a $(bold)glass break$() sound.$(br2)Blacklisted: the $(l:cursed_tool_gourd_jail)Prison Realm$() and the Iron's Spellbooks $(bold)pocket dimension$().
